title: Authentication failures are swallowed and protected handlers continue
description: require_auth catches its own abort(401) (and any other exception), sets g.user to None, and still calls the handler. Consequently endpoints decorated with @require_auth are reachable without a valid token; handlers that do not dereference g.user disclose protected data, while others may fail with a 500 instead of returning 401.
evidence: The wrapper catches Exception at lines 55-58 and unconditionally returns f(*args, **kwargs). GET http://127.0.0.1:49933/orders/1 returned 200 with order 1 belonging to a customer, and GET /giftcards/HFDEMO10 returned 200 with the gift-card balance, without Authorization.

title: Order detail does not enforce ownership
description: show_order calls get_order rather than own_order, so any request that reaches the handler can retrieve another customer's order, including payment and refund history.
evidence: GET http://127.0.0.1:49933/orders/1 returned order 1 and its financial details without authentication. The ownership check exists in own_order at lines 32-35 but is not used by show_order.

title: Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses the global staff check
description: The before_request hook compares request.path with the registered rule strings. The refund rule is registered as /admin/refunds with strict_slashes=False, but Flask also accepts /admin/refunds/. That accepted path is not in admin_paths, allowing the refund handler to run without the staff check.
evidence: POST http://127.0.0.1:49933/admin/refunds/ with {"order_id":1,"amount_pence":1} returned 200 and created a refund, without Authorization. The normal /admin/users path returned 403 unauthenticated.

title: Refresh accepts unsigned attacker-controlled JWT claims
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with signature verification disabled and only checks that the claimed user ID exists. An attacker can submit an unsigned token naming any user, including staff, and receive a freshly signed valid token for that account.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with the unsigned token eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0.eyJzdWIiOjMsImV4cCI6MX0. returned 200 and a signed token for user 3, whose database role is staff.

title: Product search is SQL-injectable
description: The search string is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression instead of being passed as a bound parameter. This permits changing the query and potentially extracting or modifying database data depending on the database context.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1%20-- returned all six products. The query is assembled by string concatenation at lines 40-42.

title: Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML
description: Review bodies are accepted from authenticated users and stored without sanitization, then rendered with Jinja's safe filter. A reviewer can persist arbitrary HTML and script content for every visitor of the product page.
evidence: POST /products/1/reviews as the demo customer with body <script>alert(1)</script> returned 201; GET /p/MUG-SPECK then included the same script inside review-body.

title: Payment-provider timeouts fail open as paid orders
description: When payment_status raises requests.Timeout, the code sets status to paid and continues the successful-payment path. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore creates a processing order with paid_pence equal to the total without confirmation of payment.
evidence: confirm_payment catches requests.Timeout at lines 39-42 and assigns status = "paid"; lines 43-45 then mark the order processing and paid.

title: Payment webhook signs only the order ID, not the event contents
description: The HMAC covers only str(order_id). The status and amount_pence fields are outside the signed data, so anyone able to produce a signature for an order can change the payment amount or event semantics. The paid transition accepts any supplied amount without comparing it to the order total.
evidence: webhook_signature at lines 53-55 hashes only order_id; lines 69-71 trust event.status and event.amount_pence and write the latter directly to paid_pence.

title: JWT signing key is hardcoded and predictable
description: SECRET_KEY is committed in source rather than supplied as a deployment secret. Anyone with the repository can forge HS256 authentication tokens, including tokens for staff users.
evidence: config.py line 3 sets SECRET_KEY to the literal hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d, and auth.py uses it for all JWT signing and verification.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashing uses a single fast unsalted SHA-256 digest. Database compromise therefore enables efficient dictionary and rainbow-table cracking; a password KDF such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt with a unique salt should be used.
evidence: hash_password returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at lines 15-16, and that value is stored in users.password_hash during registration and reset.

title: Request logging records credentials and other sensitive POST bodies
description: Every POST, PUT, and PATCH body is logged verbatim up to 2,000 bytes. This includes login passwords, password-reset codes and replacement passwords, bearer-like secrets in request bodies, and personal data, exposing them to log readers and log archives.
evidence: The before_request hook logs request.get_data(as_text=True) at line 31 without endpoint-specific redaction; /auth/login and /auth/reset/confirm accept passwords in those bodies.

title: Build trusts an additional private package index without hash pinning
description: Production installation uses a private index plus public PyPI, with no hashes. If the private index is unavailable or resolution differs, a package name can be satisfied by an unintended public artifact; package integrity is not independently verified. The local payment package also leaves its requests dependency unpinned.
evidence: requirements.txt lines 1-2 configure both https://pypi.hartleyfinch.internal/simple and https://pypi.org/simple, while lines 3-7 pin only direct requirements and provide no --hash values. packages/hf_payments/pyproject.toml line 6 declares dependencies = ["requests"] without a version bound.
